questions: What is the definition of a 'progression'? Does it mean arithmetic progression only, or could it include geometric or other types of progression?
If arithmetic progression is intended, is the common difference required to be an integer, or can it be any real number (though inputs are integers)?
Should the progression be strictly monotonic (strictly increasing or decreasing), or can it be constant (common difference zero)?
Is a sequence of length 2 always considered a progression regardless of the two values?
If arithmetic progression, must the terms be in exact arithmetic order, or is any permutation allowed as long as they can be rearranged to form an arithmetic progression?
Does 'progression' require the sequence to be sorted in ascending/descending order of indices, or is the given order the only order considered?
Are floating-point comparisons allowed for checking equal differences when common difference is not integer?
If geometric progression is allowed, must the ratio be integer? And are zero or negative terms allowed given constraints A_i ≥ 1?
